verses.text: There are mines for silver and places where people refine gold.
People dig iron out of the ground and melt copper out of its ore.
They bring light into the darkness and search as far as they can for stone buried in deep shadows.
They sink a shaft far from where people live, where no one passes by. Far from everyone, they hang and swing back and forth.
Food grows from the earth above, while underneath it the ground is torn up as if by fire.
Its rocks hold sapphires, and there is gold dust down there.
No bird of prey knows that path. Even a falcon has never spotted it.
Proud beasts have never set foot there. Even the fiercest lion has never passed that way.
People break through hard rock and overturn mountains at their roots.
They cut channels through the rock and spot every precious thing.
They dam up streams to stop the water from seeping in, and bring hidden things to light.
But where can you find wisdom? Where does understanding live?
No one knows what wisdom is worth. It cannot be found in the land of the living.
The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘I don’t have it.’
You can’t buy it with gold or weigh out enough silver to pay for it.
Even the gold of Ophir, precious onyx, and sapphire can’t match its value.
Gold and glass can’t compare to it. You can’t trade fine gold jewelry for it.
Coral and crystal aren’t even worth mentioning. Wisdom is worth more than rubies.
Topaz from Ethiopia can’t compare. Even pure gold can’t measure its worth.
So where does wisdom come from? Where does understanding live?
It’s hidden from every living eye, even from the birds overhead.
Destruction and Death say, ‘We’ve only heard rumors about it.’
God knows the way to wisdom. He knows where it lives.
He can see to the ends of the earth. He sees everything under the sky.
He set the force of the wind and measured out the waters.
He set a rule for the rain and marked out a path for the thunderbolt.
Then he saw wisdom and declared it. He established it and examined it thoroughly.
He told humanity, ‘To fear the Lord is wisdom. To turn away from evil is understanding.’
